relevance_note: Single-family case report of HA20: 'A heterozygous mutation of TNFAIP3 (c.305A>G, p. Asn 102 Ser) was identified in the patient', and the same variant in her father and brother.
method_note: Read the full paper and built the JSON by hand-entered values in a short Python script (no table transcription; the paper has no tables, and Figures 2B/2D, which hold the variant details, are not in the text). Four people recorded: the proband ('patient', also called 'the proband'), her father, her brother (called 'younger brother' once) and her pregnant sister, who was Sanger-tested and lacked the variant (no variant row, no features). The mother and 'other family members without TNFAIP3 mutation' are mentioned only collectively and get no rows. Inheritance is left 'not reported' for all carriers: the paper reports the father carries the identical variant but never states that the patient inherited it, and the mother is not named. Variant class is 'not reported' because the authors never call it missense. The STRA8 and UEVLD homozygous variants are attributed to the patient's WES unambiguously and are recorded, but the text gives no HGVS for them (only in Figure 2B), and the authors deem them non-causal. Points a reviewer should know, not strictly contradictions: the authors call c.305A>G 'novel' in HA20 yet give population frequencies (MAF=0.0079 in 1000G_EAS up to MAF=0.01734 in ExAC), say 'This mutation causes decreased A20 expression' citing ref. 10, and say 'it is also proposed as a risk factor for autoimmune disorders (11, 12)'; and the non-carrier sister also had reduced A20 by Western blot. The abstract says the father and brother had oral ulcers 'since childhood'; the case text says the father 'when he was young' and the brother 'since he was 4 years old' (recorded from the case text). Age 29 is recorded as age at last evaluation (age at report); no age at diagnosis is stated. A 'low titer' ANA (1:100) was marked observed for autoantibodies. Normal immunoglobulin levels were recorded as excluded rows (abnormal level absent). No group-statement exclusions were made.
